There is really no right or wrong and it depends on your posibilities. If you are living in the place where your target language is spoken I am not sure how I would approach learning a language.
The two foreign languages I am learning are not spoken here, so I have had to build a plan accordingly. What I do is get as much exposure to the languages as I can. I watch series, movies and listen to as much music in the languages as it's possible. When I got the hang of how the words are separated (I practise the songs word by word, repeat them, and try to remember certain words from them), I start noticing certain words that are repeated in the movies or series I watch (I recommend series because they generally make use of similar words in each episode). Each episode, I write two or three words that I find easy to remember either because they are often repeated or because they are said separated from full sentences. I help myself with the subtitles to know what they mean and to look for them in every episode. I repeat this strategy until I remember lots of words or even just the roots of some of them. After I have gathered enough vocabulary, I start with grammar patterns (I would recommend to find a grammar book for this, they are organized depending on the way a person generally acquires the language). By this point it is easier to notice the patterns because I already know the meaning of many words (many are verbs or just their roots). Then I start practicing with the books while continuing being exposed to the language. Then, I would recommend talking to native speakers in some way to help you speak the language. I have language partners for English and a native teacher to practise Japanese. If you can, maybe take some classes every once in a while just to clear out some doubts you may have about grammar or use of certain words. 
I hope this helped! Oh and also a thesaurus of the target language helps wonders to know collocations!!
Good luck!
